To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified an intermediate phenotype for schizophrenia in unaffected first degree relatives that was significantly correlated with trait anxiety, test retest reliable, task specific for emotional face processing, and associated with the illness.
we have identified a functional connectomic phenotype for schizophrenia that includes a subnetwork of visual and limbic brain regions and that is related to emotional face processing.

a graph theoretical approach identified significantly decreased functional connectivity in a sub-network that primarily included the visual, limbic and subcortical regions during emotional face processing in unaffected relatives of schizophrenia patients compared with healthy controls and that this connectivity was also decreased in patients with manifest schizophrenia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of emotional face processing.
the neural mechanisms underlying the genetic risk for schizophrenia.
identifying neural mechanisms that may contribute to the genetic risk of schizophrenia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current results indicate that altered limbic visual connectivity during emotional face processing in unaffected relatives of patients with SZ and in SZ patients is a promising intermediate phenotype.

the results of the present study are consistent with a model of schizophrenia in which there is a genetic predisposition to altered connectivity in a limbic visual subnetwork during emotional processing.

the study identified a subnetwork of brain regions involved in emotional processing that was altered in schizophrenia patients and unaffected relatives, and that this alteration may be an intermediate phenotype for schizophrenia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current results provide a potential systems level connectomic intermediate phenotype that is associated with the genetic liability for schizophrenia and may have clinical validity.
a functional connectomic phenotype for schizophrenia can be identified and that it is related to the clinical state of patients.

we have identified a functional subnetwork during emotional processing that is altered in relatives of patients with Schizophrenia, is test retest reliable, is related to trait anxiety and is related to clinical symptoms of schizophrenia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the functional connectome is likely a more informative measure of neural dysfunction in schizophrenia than regional activity or regional connectivity.
we have found a functional connectome biomarker for schizophrenia that is reliable, heritable, related to anxiety, and related to manifest illness.

a systems level analysis of functional connectivity during emotional face processing in schizophrenia and unaffected first degree relatives identified a potential intermediate phenotype that may be a promising target for future clinical studies.
